text:
maria: onboarding note — ACME Private: we need to finalize the AWS KMS approach for control-plane + data-plane encryption. main Qs: do they BYOK both, or do we manage control-plane CMK and allow BYOK for dataplane? also: recommended encryption-context keys, DEK cache TTL, and rewrap/rotation flow. cc @samir @jake

samir: suggest pattern we used for beta customers: control-plane keys live in customer account (BYOK) when they require full custody. we create cross-account IAM roles and use KMS grants for the redwood-controlplane role to GenerateDataKey/Decrypt/ReEncrypt. advantage: customer retains audit in their CloudTrail + key rotation control. downside: cross-account grants are a bit fiddly and need grant lifetime management.

jake: two practical options: 1) Customer-managed CMK in their account (recommended for regulated customers). we only ask for the CMK ARN and an IAM role to assume. 2) Redwood-managed CMK in Redwood account with a strict key policy + audit export to the customer (less ideal for compliance).

alice: about encryption context: we must bind DEKs to tenant and scope. propose: {"tenant_id": "<TENANT>", "resource": "redwood:dataplane"} for data-plane keys and "redwood:controlplane" for control-plane ops. encryption-context should be required in the grant constraint to prevent re-use.

jake: sample create-grant command (cross-account):
```
aws kms create-grant \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-1234 \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-controlplane \
  --operations Encrypt Decrypt ReEncrypt GenerateDataKey \
  --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"tenant_id":"acme-corp"}
```

maria: DEK caching: what's reasonable TTL? we want to avoid re-decrypting every request but also honor rotation quickly.

samir: 5–15 minutes is typical for high-throughput services. we stash DEKs in an encrypted in-memory cache keyed by (tenant_id, key_version). on CMK rotation, we set a short-lived rewrap window: old DEKs remain usable for 1 hour then background rewrap job re-encrypts active DEKs with new CMK. for strict compliance customers we do immediate rewrap on next access and log events.

ops: reminder: if customer supplies CMK and wants VPC-only access, they must allow the redwood-controlplane role principal and also configure an interface VPC endpoint for KMS in their VPC if calls originate from a private network. also ensure KMS key policy has sts:AssumeRole principals for our cross-account role.

security-bot: added runbook link and minimal key policy snippet to the channel docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-byok-onboarding
Key policy example we use (minimal):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "AllowUseFromCustomerAdmin", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"}, "Action": "kms:*", "Resource": "*" },
    { "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-controlplane"}, "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncryptFrom","kms:Encrypt"], "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:tenant_id": "acme-corp"}} }
  ]
}
```

alice: audit / CloudTrail: confirm we get decrypt/generate-data-key events in customer account if CMK is BYOK, which they want for compliance. we should also stream our own control-plane events to their SIEM if they request.

maria: thanks — action items: 1) samir to draft onboarding checklist for BYOK (policy snippet, required roles, example aws cli commands). 2) jake to add encryption-context validation to the control-plane client (reject calls missing tenant_id). 3) ops to validate VPC endpoint docs. 4) alice to add rotation rewrap job notes to runbook. target: have docs + checklist ready before next onboarding call (tomorrow 9am PT). :thumbsup:
